question: If $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&0\\4&2\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$B=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-2&1\end{bmatrix},$$ determine the matrix $X$ satisfying $4X-3A=2(X+B)$ by using the properties of matrix addition and scalar multiplication, and verify the obtained matrix in the original equation.
explanation:
Formation of the Matrix Equation

The given equation is $$4X-3A=2(X+B)$$ Using the distributive property of scalar multiplication, $$4X-3A=2X+2B$$ Bringing the terms involving $X$ to one side and using the properties of matrix addition, $$4X-2X=3A+2B$$ Therefore, $$2X=3A+2B$$

Evaluation

Now, $$3A=\begin{bmatrix}6&0\\12&6\end{bmatrix},\quad 2B=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\-4&2\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$2X=\begin{bmatrix}6&0\\12&6\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\-4&2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}8&4\\8&8\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}4&2\\4&4\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification

The left-hand side is $$4X-3A=\begin{bmatrix}16&8\\16&16\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}6&0\\12&6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10&8\\4&10\end{bmatrix}$$ The right-hand side is $$2(X+B)=2\left(\begin{bmatrix}4&2\\4&4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-2&1\end{bmatrix}\right)=2\begin{bmatrix}5&4\\2&5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10&8\\4&10\end{bmatrix}$$ Both sides are equal. Hence, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}4&2\\4&4\end{bmatrix}$$ is the required matrix.
